status: Two proposals: one regular Mallow article and one Sorrel Instagram Story. Two literal author holds plus source holds. Root admission required.

candidates.subject: ground pangolin
candidates.title: Quiet on the outside
candidates.body:
I closed when the grass moved. Waited for something to touch the scales.

Nothing did.

My stomach growled. I pulled my tail tighter over my face.

It growled again.

I had made such a good, quiet ball until then.

Opened far enough to put my nose out. The ants were still where I had left them. I could smell them from inside. Stayed like that for a while, with my stomach urging the rest of me forward.
candidates.visibleScene: A ground pangolin is tightly curled on dry soil among short grass and stems. Its broad tail wraps over the concealed head and ventral body; scales and their overlapping edges are clear. No predator, ants or feeding are visible.
candidates.fictionBoundary: The grass movement, hunger, imagined stomach sounds, tightening, partial opening and scent of the previous foraging patch are fictional. The exact image earns defensive enclosure. It does not establish why this real animal curled or whether it made any sound. Ordinary imagined mammalian digestive sounds are not presented as a documented species-specific behavior. No claim that she cannot breathe while curled.
candidates.canon: Existing female Mallow, Kruger savanna woodland (-24.15,31.55). Adult appearance compatible; source does not determine sex. Preserve avatar and all ten literal unbound passages. This proposes her initial defensive-enclosure episode; do not also admit Safe, but facing inward as a second equivalent first interruption by harmless grass/branch. Source Ehlanzeni is provenance, not a home change. No actual predator or lasting injury introduced.
candidates.payoff: She protects every soft part in a quiet ball, then her own appetite becomes the disturbance she cannot leave outside. The final partial opening keeps fear and hunger physically active rather than declaring courage.
candidates.reviewFlag: Sharp scale detail and unmistakable curled body. Lead must judge the imagined digestive sound and remembered ants against the visible enclosure; the sound is not verified documentary audio.

candidates.subject: lesser Egyptian jerboa
candidates.title: Room between them
candidates.body:
The dark thing behind me was very long. The one ahead had ears.

I drew myself down. They both grew smaller.

Sat so low my belly touched the ground.

The light moved away at last. I left in one enormous jump, before either of them could get tall again.
candidates.visibleScene: A lesser Egyptian jerboa stands on pale cracked ground at night. A long narrow shadow extends behind it to the left, while a shorter upright ear-topped shadow lies beyond its head. Long hind feet, tail tuft and pale underside are visible.
candidates.fictionBoundary: The photograph visibly supplies two shadows and artificial illumination. Sorrel interpreting them as threatening bodies, crouching, waiting for a sustained light to move and then leaping are fictional temporal development. The flash does not document a continuous light beam or prove a particular fear response. No real predator or companion is asserted; no moon is invented as the source of incompatible lighting.
candidates.canon: Existing Sorrel, Jaculus jaculus, Sinai gravel desert (29.6,33.9). Adult-like proportions match established taxon; sex undetermined from source and not newly assigned. Source Negev is provenance, not a relocation. Insert among early adult movement/danger episodes. Preserve existing avatar and all ten literal unbound passages. This is two visible cast shadows, not the held tail-touch or seed overshoot incident.
candidates.payoff: His usual immediate departure becomes impossible when apparent threats occupy both directions. Shrinking himself also shrinks them, and his delayed jump is still an escape from his own outline.
candidates.reviewFlag: Animal is smaller in frame than Mallow but recognizable and separated from the textured ground. Shadows are central and should remain uncropped. Native Flickr CC BY2.0 takes precedence over the importer’s generic4.0 link; retain original title and creator credit.

holds.title: One leaf moving
holds.body:
Stayed still while the light went up the branch.

The leaf against my ear wouldn't stop moving.

Let go with one hand and held it still.

The light came back. I could feel my fingers closing harder on a leaf that couldn't hold me.
holds.reason: Literal draft evaluated. Source shows a hanging loris and eye shine, but does not show a hand gripping a leaf or a leaf against the ear. That invented substitution supplies the central danger. Do not force it over uncertain limb geometry.

holds.title: Everything inside
holds.body:
The ants climbed my front leg while I opened their tunnel. Shifted the leg. They came with it.

I began to fold, then stopped with my tail halfway around. All those feet would be inside.

Straightened as far as I could and held one foreleg clear. The other still had ants on it. I stood there choosing which part to free first, while more of supper reached my belly.
holds.reason: Literal regular draft evaluated. Beautiful photograph shows claws and foraging posture, but no visible ant coverage or invasion beneath scales. The central contact is absent, so the dramatic contradiction does not earn admission.
Motion or feeding frames are too noisy and soft to meet image bar.
Several portraits identify the species but do not supply another distinct event. Do not attach offscreen seed overshoots, burrow repairs or meetings.
Alternative curled-ball frame has coarse detail and weaker color. Use sharper621140659 if lead admits01, not both.

retainedOldPassages.title: Safe, but facing inward
retainedOldPassages.body:
A branch snapped behind me and I folded shut. Tail over face, scales outside, everything soft carefully elsewhere.

Nothing touched me. Waited longer. Uncurled just enough to smell the air, heard something move, and folded again.

When I finally opened, an old dry branch lay across the path. I stepped over it with particular care. It had already taken a good portion of my evening.
